dimensions.assessment: Affects pediatric cancer patients, drug manufacturers, organ procurement organizations, and participants in federal health research programs.
Imposes new study requirements and enforcement mechanisms on drug sponsors, alters market exclusivity interpretations, and adjusts a Medicare fund by over one billion dollars.
Increases authorized funding for the Medicare Improvement Fund by $1.219 billion and authorizes $25 million annually for FY2026-FY2028 for pediatric studies.
Amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act, the Public Health Service Act, and the Social Security Act across multiple distinct programs.
Contains permanent statutory adjustments alongside specific authorizations and sunset provisions ranging from 3 to 10 years.

missing_information: Detailed economic forecasts regarding the commercial impact of modified orphan drug exclusivity rules.
importance_detail.rationale: Expands FDA authority over pediatric cancer research and rare pediatric diseases, reauthorizes priority review vouchers, modifies orphan drug exclusivity rules, adjusts Medicare Improvement Fund spending, and establishes an Abraham Accords Office.

card.summary: H.R. 7148, titled the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026, became Public Law No. 119-75 on February 3, 2026. This federal law provides funding for the Department of Defense, Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, and Education, as well as Transportation, Housing and Urban Development, and related agencies for fiscal year 2026. It also sets guidelines for the U.S. Sentencing Commission, extends various healthcare, Medicaid, Medicare, and trade programs, introduces pharmacy benefit management transparency rules, and awards a payment to the widow of a late representative.
card.title: Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026

card.summary: The Mikaela Naylon Give Kids a Chance Act of 2025 amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to authorize targeted clinical trials using combinations of drugs for pediatric cancer. It also renews the Food and Drug Administration's authority to issue priority review vouchers for sponsors of new products intended to treat rare pediatric diseases until September 30, 2030, and requires the Government Accountability Office and the Department of Health and Human Services to submit reports on the implementation and effectiveness of these provisions.
